task.title: Install BPM from source on Fedora Linux 44
task.shortdesc: Run the complete BPM 0.9.1 source-install sequence on Fedora Linux 44 with its distribution Python 3.14 runtime.

prereq.p: Use Fedora Linux 44 with sudo access, outbound HTTPS, and an approved BPM 0.9.1 Git ref.

context.p: This is a foreground single-node source workflow, not a systemd or production deployment recipe.

info.codeblock: . /etc/os-release test "$ID" = "fedora" && test "$VERSION_ID" = "44" sudo dnf install -y ca-certificates curl gcc gcc-c++ git make python3 python3-devel export BPM_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 "$BPM_PYTHON" --version

step.cmd: Check out the approved BPM source ref.

info.codeblock: export BPM_REPOSITORY_URL="https://github.com/Goudron/browser-policy-manager.git" export BPM_REF="<approved-0.9.1-ref>" test "$BPM_REF" != "<approved-0.9.1-ref>" cd "$HOME" git clone "$BPM_REPOSITORY_URL" browser-policy-manager cd "$HOME/browser-policy-manager" git checkout --detach "$BPM_REF" git status --short git rev-parse --short HEAD

step.cmd: Create the environment, install BPM, and migrate.

info.codeblock: "$BPM_PYTHON" -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install --upgrade pip pip install -e ".[dev]" python --version mkdir -p data export BPM_DATABASE_URL="sqlite+aiosqlite:///./data/bpm.db" alembic upgrade head
export BPM_HOST="127.0.0.1" export BPM_PORT="8000" export BPM_RELOAD="true" make dev
info.p: Use a second terminal for checks.

step.cmd: Verify probes, UI, and foreground logs.

info.codeblock: cd browser-policy-manager source .venv/bin/activate curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/health curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/ready curl -fsS -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8000/profiles

info.p: On failure, press Ctrl+C, preserve DNF, pip, migration, build, probe, and log evidence, and do not run alembic downgrade.

result.p: The Fedora Linux 44 host has a migrated BPM source checkout, passing probes, responding UI, and foreground logs.

postreq.p: The command sequence passed in a clean Fedora 44 userspace container. This evidence does not verify native boot, kernel, systemd, desktop, hardware, host firewall, or production deployment.
